## Criterion and masked metadata

A file is reproduced if it is byte-identical to the committed version, or if JSON and Markdown reports differ only in run metadata: the JSON keys `duration_seconds_total`, `durations`, `elapsed_seconds`, `git_commit`, `git_dirty`, `integration_tests`, `model_load_seconds`, `platform`, `run_info`, `seconds`, `test_output`, `timestamp_utc`, `timing`, `timings`, `wall_seconds`; in Markdown, the generated-by line (commit, dirty flag, time), the integration-test summary line, model loading time, git commit hashes (40 hex digits; SHA-256 checksums stay compared) and the sections `## Run`, `## Timing`. Everything else (scores, tables, figures, manifests, captions) must be byte-identical; there is no numerical tolerance.

Nondeterminism observed: only run metadata (timestamps, commit hashes, including the commit recorded for an upstream input table, the dirty flag, which is true for every step after the first because earlier steps rewrite tracked files, durations, and the platform string, which records the OS version).
